# Protected workflow entry point

The [qualification workflow](../workflows/evidencehost-protected-parent.yml) runs only through `workflow_dispatch` on protected `main` in `forge-trust/AppSurface`. Its only input is a reviewed record identifier. It checks out the workflow's own immutable revision with persisted credentials disabled, builds the [semantic consumer](semantic-gate/README.md) and its protected dependencies, and passes the read-only API token only to the final parent process. It never checks out or evaluates the candidate subject. A branch copy of this workflow is not protected acceptance.

`entrypoint.run_reviewed_record(record_id, environment, token, *, dotnet_host, checkout_head, total_timeout=150)` compares the provider repository/ref/protection/event/workflow facts, the checked-out Git head, and both `GITHUB_SHA` and `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA`. The workflow path must be this fixed workflow on `main`. `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA` is a source commit, not a workflow-file digest. Local callers can forge environment variables; these comparisons gain meaning only inside the independently reviewed workflow and repository protection configuration.

The fixed [`protected-records.json`](protected-records.json) has schema `issue779-protected-parent-records-v1` and a `records` array of at most 64 entries, each with exactly `id`, `context_sha256` and numeric `repository_id`. An identifier is 1–64 lowercase ASCII letters/digits/hyphens, beginning with a letter or digit. It selects only `records/<id>.json`; no caller or record can select a URL, filename, executable or arguments. The file must be a stable single-link regular file with the reviewed SHA-256 and the [dispatch context](dispatch-README.md#closed-context-format), at most 24 MiB. Registry JSON rejects duplicate/case-aliased members. A context contains original policy/diff bytes, expected identities and actual collected artifact bodies, not manifest digests in place of those bodies.

Before dispatch, the entry point reads authenticated repository metadata from the fixed GitHub API endpoint and requires the exact repository ID/name and `default_branch=main`. A protected ref alone does not establish that it is the canonical default branch or that required-review policy is configured. Repository metadata resolution and the semantic dispatch share the original 150-second entry-point deadline; neither creates a fresh budget.

The registry is currently empty. Every identifier therefore rejects before resolver, API or semantic-child I/O. A maintainer must independently review and commit an exact completed producer run/attempt, workflow bytes, source/base, artifact ID/API digest/bytes, expected gate facts and collected bodies before adding a record. The producer run must already be completed successfully: the resolver cannot require completion of the consumer's own still-running workflow. No “latest” lookup or artifact-name discovery is used. Protecting the workflow, review rules and record is a repository/release responsibility, not a fact proved by public JSON or a local environment flag.

The [resolver](github-parent-README.md) authenticates exact GitHub metadata and verifies the fixed archive before selecting plan and manifest; [dispatch](dispatch-README.md) reconstructs the semantic envelope and supervises the fixed child under its original deadline. The child receives no API token. A zero exit prints `EVIDENCE_PROTECTED_PARENT_SEMANTIC_ALLOWED` and means only that the reviewed semantic inputs satisfied the existing public gate. Denied inputs and malformed/unregistered contexts emit fixed diagnostics without paths, raw subject bytes or token values.

This qualification entry point creates no admission and does not enable Trusted. The production catalogue and accepted-consumer registry remain closed pending the actual isolation, CLI/SDK, downstream and release acceptance in the [consumer record](../../docs/evidence/issue779-consumer-acceptance.md) and [test plan](../../docs/plans/issue-779-evidencehost-test-plan.md). The workflow must first be reviewed and merged onto protected `main`; executing a candidate branch version cannot substitute for that step. Detached tests verify selection and rejection ordering only.
